script: One American soldier once captured 132 enemy troops by himself, using skills he learned hunting turkey back home. In October 1918, Corporal Alvin York, a sharpshooter from the Tennessee mountains, was part of a small patrol sent to silence a German machine gun position in France. The patrol walked into an ambush, and half the men went down in seconds. With his commanding officers killed, York took charge alone. He picked off enemy gunners one by one with precise rifle fire, using turkey calling techniques from his childhood to draw them out. When a group of German soldiers charged him with bayonets, he dropped them one at a time, back to front, so the ones ahead never saw it coming. The German commander, convinced he was facing an entire company, surrendered his unit on the spot. York walked out of the forest with 132 prisoners and just seven of his own men. He was awarded the Medal of Honor, and became one of the most decorated American soldiers of the entire war. One American soldier once captured 132 enemy troops by himself, and came home a legend.
